mechanism_summary: A provisional pattern exists among false-negative large winners: muted 20-day momentum, below-average short-term volume expansion, and modest extension above the trigger. One case resembles a quiet drift with missing pullback fields, while the other shows an eight-week shallow pullback, so the cases share some state features but not a clearly coherent structural profile. The frozen data contains no industry-membership, sector-flow, sector-relative-strength, or portfolio-capacity variables, so industry concentration cannot be identified as the causal mechanism. Repeatedness is also unestablished because only two entities meet the explicit false-negative-big-winner definition, and the broader false-negative group contains losses and small winners. Any policy should therefore be framed as a constrained out-of-sample experiment, not as evidence that a sector-driven quiet-base precursor has been discovered.
falsifiers: On a chronological held-out sample, the proposed low-momentum and low-volume precursor does not achieve a large-win rate or lift above the unconditional non-pick large-win base rate at a prespecified coverage level.

Within the same held-out snapshots, adding industry-concentration or sector-relative-strength confirmation does not improve ranking, coverage, calibration, or large-win precision beyond the stock-level precursor variables alone.
After null pullback fields are excluded, the three observed false-negative big winners do not form a more coherent base structure than matched non-pick controls.

Prospectively relaxing the B0 thresholds captures the expected additional winners but produces a statistically or economically material increase in losses, ruins, or drawdowns that offsets the recovered winners.
The apparent signature disappears when snapshot clustering, regime, industry, or exposure concentration is added as a fixed effect or when the comparison is restricted to contemporaneous candidates.
A materially larger discovery set contains no recurring cell characterized by low mom_20, low vol_ratio_5_20, and small extension above the trigger among false-negative large winners.
Capacity-aware backtests show that the proposed candidates cannot be entered or exited at the modeled prices after spreads, liquidity constraints, position limits, and turnover are applied.
actionable_design_principles: Treat null pullback observations as unknown rather than evidence of a quiet or extended base; preserve missingness and use null-aware branches or explicit non-null analyses.

Define industry concentration prospectively using only PIT-available industry classification and contemporaneous sector breadth, flow, dispersion, or relative-strength measures; do not infer it from a selected-winner count alone.
Use chronological, snapshot-grouped validation to prevent the two large-winner false negatives in snap_71486ed83c from determining rules that are then evaluated on the same snapshot.
Evaluate the stock-level precursor jointly against matched non-picks and false-positive ruins, reporting large-win lift, loss capture, precision, coverage, and calibration rather than case anecdotes.
Require sector confirmation before relaxing B0 momentum thresholds; do not deploy the relaxation as an unconditional low-momentum screen.

Separate stock-selection rules from portfolio construction by testing expected alpha and hit rate first, then applying liquidity, participation, volatility, correlation, and capacity constraints in a second stage.
Prefer continuous ranking or partial dependence analysis over a hard composite whose thresholds can be satisfied on opposite sides of nearly every cutoff.
Freeze all features, transformations, null handling, snapshot definitions, and candidate-universe rules before examining the held-out outcomes.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Define a null-aware quiet-drift candidate branch requiring low mom_20, low vol_ratio_5_20, and small ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct, but only permit relaxed eligibility when a contemporaneous PIT sector-confirmation condition is active.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This captures the recurring weak individual-confirmation pattern without converting missing pullback data into a positive structural signal and without asserting that industry concentration is already measured.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Initially cap exposure using existing liquidity and volatility limits; sector confirmation must not bypass capacity checks. Estimate impact and achievable position size in the execution-stage backtest.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Create a shallow-pullback branch for candidates with observed pullback data and prohibit inference when pullback_duration_weeks or pullback_pct is null.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: The observed eight-week, minus-7.3% pullback is one of the few concrete structural precedents, but another big winner has no observed pullback record, making null-sensitive branching essential.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Use branch-specific position limits because shallow, longer-duration structures may carry different gap, turnover, and exit-liquidity behavior from confirmed breakouts.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Run an out-of-sample regime-overlay experiment that compares relaxed and baseline B0 rules within strata defined by contemporaneous sector breadth, sector dispersion, and sector relative strength.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: This tests whether any incremental value is genuinely attributable to an industry-concentration regime rather than merely replicating a stock-level quiet-drift effect.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Measure whether the overlay changes portfolio concentration, turnover, and drawdown after industry and position caps; predictive lift alone is insufficient for deployment.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Replace the hard composite with a monotonic precursor score validated for incremental lift over snapshot, industry, momentum, and volatility baselines.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: A continuous score avoids dependence on arbitrary joint cutoffs and directly tests whether the apparent pattern generalizes beyond two heterogeneous big winners.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Translate scores into positions only after applying liquidity, participation, volatility, and concentration constraints; keep score generation independent of portfolio-size rules.

dsl_policy_ideas.idea: Add a ruin-contamination gate that requires the candidate to beat matched weak-momentum ruins on structure, breadth, or sector confirmation before inclusion.
dsl_policy_ideas.why_distinct: The frozen ruins overlap the proposed quiet signature, so the gate tests whether structural or regime information can distinguish latent large winners from adverse low-momentum names rather than celebrating winner recall alone.
dsl_policy_ideas.capacity_relevance: Require lower turnover and smaller initial sizing for any branch that remains materially exposed to ruin outcomes, with promotion based on incremental risk-adjusted capacity rather than hit rate.
